3.text: residence is to be made, all the antlers except the largest are left behind.

4.text: Those are taken away to be used for monuments to the dead. A set of large

5.text: antlers is sometimes attached to the end of a long pole made fast in the ground.

6.text: This is intended as a special offering to the Upper Being or to the zenith.

7.text: The antlers of wild reindeer-bucks killed on the hunt, which are larger than

8.text: those of domesticated animals, are preferred for marking burial-places. All

9.text: the antlers of domesticated animals slaughtered on ceremonial days must be

10.text: left behind when the residence is moved.

11.text: Besides slaughtered reindeer and dogs, the Chukchee offer several other

12.text: kinds of sacrifice to the “spirits.” First among these should

13.text: be mentioned the “substitute” offerings, which are small

14.text: figures shaped like reindeer, and made of tallow, pounded

15.text: meat, crushed willow-leaves, edible plants and roots (Fig.

16.text: 263, a), or even snow (Fig. 263, b). The fœtuses extracted
